description: Deterministic synthetic fixtures for the M3-07 multi-cue/multi-occurrence integration suite (tests/test_multi_cue_analysis.py), exercising the existing, unmodified M3-03/M3-05 orchestration entry point (run_multi_cue_analysis, src/audio_cue_locator/application/multi_cue_orchestration.py) and, through it, the existing unmodified M2-02 baseline matcher (match_cue, src/audio_cue_locator/infrastructure/acoustic_matching/baseline.py), which this manifest does not redefine. Every array is a plain list of finite floats; the consuming test converts each to a CANONICAL_AUDIO_SPEC-conformant (mono, float32) numpy array itself -- this manifest does not declare its own sample rate, since the canonical sample rate (48000 Hz) is owned by CANONICAL_AUDIO_SPEC and must not be duplicated here, mirroring tests/fixtures/matching/manifest.json's own convention. This manifest extends that same synthetic finite-float-array fixture lineage to a multi-cue Analysis (a source paired with more than one cue, per run_multi_cue_analysis's own (source, cues, configuration) signature) rather than reusing the M1-era real media files under tests/fixtures/ (sine_440hz_mono_1s.wav, video_with_audio.mp4, no_audio_stream.mp4, not_media.txt): those exist to exercise M1's canonicalization/probing error handling (tests/test_canonicalization_fixtures.py's own module docstring) and carry no documented cue occurrence, ground-truth position, or absence label, and tests/fixtures/matching/representative-manifest.json already recorded this identical 'not_reused' reasoning, plus this environment's confirmed FFmpeg/FFprobe unavailability, for the same 'reuse or extend the M1 audio/video fixtures' formal-issue language.

configuration_used_for_expected_values.note: Every expected value below was computed against this exact configuration object; a consuming test must reuse DEFAULT_CONFIGURATION unchanged, per docs/multi-cue-orchestration.md's requirement that run_multi_cue_analysis be called with a caller-supplied EffectiveConfiguration, never a module-level default read internally.

provenance.reuse_rights_statement: No external representative-media asset is used anywhere in this manifest. Every source and cue array is a deterministic, synthetically constructed finite-float list embedded directly as plain-list sample data, exactly as tests/fixtures/matching/manifest.json and tests/fixtures/matching/representative-manifest.json already do. No third-party reuse-rights, licensing, or attribution obligation applies to any asset in this manifest.
provenance.generation_method: Authored once via a private Python script that imports the existing, unmodified match_cue baseline directly (no repository files were modified by that script) to compute and verify each case's per-cue outcome/score/timestamp_seconds/diagnostic_best_score against the real algorithm, mirroring tests/fixtures/matching/representative-manifest.json's own recorded authoring methodology. This is fixture-authoring tooling, not test execution: tests/test_multi_cue_analysis.py independently re-invokes run_multi_cue_analysis (and, through it, match_cue) at test time and asserts against these same documented values; no pytest run was performed while authoring this manifest.
provenance.verification_note: Case 2's cue arrays are additively overlaid over a shared span of one source (see case_id cross_cue_temporal_overlap), so their resulting best-candidate positions were determined by the real correlation search, not by the offsets used to construct the source; the recorded expected_per_cue_outcomes below are the actual verified match_cue/run_multi_cue_analysis output for that exact source and those exact cue arrays, not a hand-derived approximation.

cases.description: One Analysis with three cues against a single shared source containing one embedded burst: two independent cue_ids ('cue-repeat-first', 'cue-repeat-second') submit the identical cue array and must each independently resolve to their own accepted occurrence at the same position with the same score (repeated cue, acceptance criterion 1) -- attribution must follow cue_id, not array identity or iteration order, per docs/multi-cue-orchestration.md. A third cue_id ('cue-absent') submits the exact phase-inversion of the embedded burst (same shape and energy, opposite sign): at the burst's own position this scores a perfect negative correlation, and everywhere else in the source the window is silent (baseline.py's deterministic 0.0 fallback for a zero-energy window), so the maximum score across the whole source is 0.0, strictly below DEFAULT_CONFIGURATION's 0.75 threshold -- a deterministic no_match (absent cue, acceptance criterion 1), not a near-miss.

One Analysis with two distinct cues ('cue-overlap-b', 'cue-overlap-c') against a single shared source in which both cues' waveforms are additively overlaid over a common span, simulating overlapping acoustic events. This is the required overlap/near-duplicate case, scoped exclusively to two distinct cues whose accepted occurrences overlap in time (docs/occurrence-temporal-semantics-and-policy.md fixes the current normalized_cross_correlation_v1 matcher at 0..1 occurrence per cue per call and states explicitly that occurrences of different cues are never grouped or deduplicated against each other, even when they overlap): each cue is independently matched with its own best-candidate position and score by run_multi_cue_analysis's per-cue call to the existing, unmodified match_cue, and both are accepted (found) at positions whose sample windows -- [best_index, best_index + len(cue)) -- intersect. Neither cue is asserted to produce more than one occurrence: this case never exercises same-cue multiplicity, which the current matcher does not support.

expected_overlap.note: best_index values are derived by the consuming test as round(temporal_position * CANONICAL_AUDIO_SPEC.sample_rate_hz); recorded here for traceability of this manifest's own authoring verification, not as a value the test must read from JSON.
